message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.11","text":"And in prayers one must also confess that one has taken refuge in God and solemnly affirm that, on the demon’s part, it is not disobedience but delay. For everything comes to pass for the one who believes, but nothing for the one who does not believe. Hence the demons themselves, knowing the quantity of faith possessed by those whom they overpower, allot a proportionate measure of their own persistence. For this reason they persist with those who do not believe, linger with those who have difficulty believing, but cannot remain even for an instant with those who have believed completely and act well. For the soul, having been turned by faith toward God as though into the nature of water, extinguishes the demon like a spark of fire. It is therefore difficult for each person to recognize the flight of the demon within them. For by blending themselves with souls, the demons suggest to each person’s mind thoughts directed toward whatever they wish, so that the person neglects their own salvation.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διαμαρτύρεσθαι τὴν τοῦ δαίμονος οὐκ ἀπείθειαν, ἀλλὰ βραδυτῆτα","chosen":"solemnly affirm that, on the demon’s part, it is not disobedience but delay","rationale":"The contrast concerns the demon’s delayed departure rather than outright refusal; “solemnly affirm” preserves the emphatic force of διαμαρτύρεσθαι."},{"source_quote":"ἀναλογοῦσαν ἐπιμετροῦσιν αὐτῶν τὴν ἐπιμονήν","chosen":"allot a proportionate measure of their own persistence","rationale":"The following clauses describe how long the demons persist according to the victim’s degree of faith. Grammatically αὐτῶν could instead refer to the people, but that gives a poorer contextual connection."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς δὲ δυσπίστοις ἐνβραδύνουσιν","chosen":"linger with those who have difficulty believing","rationale":"δύσπιστος denotes difficulty or reluctance in believing, distinguished here from outright unbelief."},{"source_quote":"κάματος οὖν ἐστὶν ἑκάστῳ ἐννοηθῆναι τὴν τοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ δαίμονος φυγήν","chosen":"It is therefore difficult for each person to recognize the flight of the demon within them","rationale":"κάματος presents the recognition as laborious or difficult; ἐννοηθῆναι can mean to perceive or recognize mentally."},{"source_quote":"ἐνθυμήσεις πρὸς ἃ βούλονται","chosen":"thoughts directed toward whatever they wish","rationale":"The phrase describes thoughts oriented toward the demons’ purposes, rather than merely thoughts that the demons happen to desire."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.12","text":"Hence many, not knowing the source by which they are being acted upon, assent to the evil notions suggested by demons as though these were the reasoning of their own soul. Therefore they become more reluctant to go to those capable of saving them, and those people, while being consumed by the very demons lying in wait for them, remain unaware. The demons lurking in the innermost recesses of their souls prompt them to suppose that it is not a demon troubling them but a bodily disease—such as acrid matter, bile, phlegm, an imbalance of blood, inflammation of the meninges, or something else—. . . . But even if this were so, not even that is exempt from being a form of demon. For the universal and earthy soul, which passes through all foods as their cause, when taken in to a greater extent through more abundant food, itself unites with the spirit as something kindred to it—the spirit being the soul of a human being—while the material portion of the food, once united with the body, is smeared upon it like a terrible poison. Therefore self-sufficiency is good in everything.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ταῖς τῶν δαιμόνων κακαῖς ὑποβαλλομέναις ἐπινοίαις ὡς τῷ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτῶν λογισμῷ συντίθενται","chosen":"assent to the evil notions suggested by demons as though these were the reasoning of their own soul","rationale":"συντίθενται means agreeing or assenting, while ὑποβαλλομέναις identifies the notions as suggestions implanted by demons."},{"source_quote":"ἐνδομυχούντων δαιμόνων","chosen":"demons lurking in the innermost recesses of their souls","rationale":"ἐνδομυχέω depicts dwelling or hiding deep within an interior recess."},{"source_quote":"ὕλης δριμείας","chosen":"acrid matter","rationale":"In the medical list ὕλη denotes bodily matter or material; “acrid humor” is also possible but would specify a technical humoral sense not explicit in the noun itself."},{"source_quote":"οὐδὲ αὐτὸ ἀπήλλακται δαίμονος εἶδος εἶναι","chosen":"not even that is exempt from being a form of demon","rationale":"The referent is most naturally the proposed bodily disease. The wording preserves the author’s claim without harmonizing it with later medical or theological categories."},{"source_quote":"ἡ γὰρ καθόλου καὶ γεώδης ψυχή","chosen":"the universal and earthy soul","rationale":"καθόλου and γεώδης characterize this soul as universal and earth-associated. “General terrestrial soul” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"διὸ ἐπὶ πάντων καλὸν ἡ αὐτάρκεια","chosen":"Therefore self-sufficiency is good in everything","rationale":"αὐτάρκεια literally denotes sufficiency or self-sufficiency; in this dietary context it may imply contentment or moderation, but the broader wording is retained."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ τοὺς ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐνεδρευόντων δαιμόνων ἀναλισκόμενοι ἀγνοοῦσιν","issue":"The accusative article τοὺς does not agree with the nominative participle ἀναλισκόμενοι or straightforwardly serve as the subject of ἀγνοοῦσιν. The translation treats τοὺς resumptively as referring to the same people and renders the participle circumstantially. Conjectures such as changing τοὺς or changing ἀναλισκόμενοι are possible, but none is required to obtain a defensible contextual sense.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἢ ἄλλου τινός) . . . .","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna marked by exactly four dots. Its content is unavailable, and no restoration has been supplied; the same four-dot gap remains explicit in the translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.13","text":"Some of the wicked demons lie in wait in another way. At first they do not even reveal that they exist, so that no effort against them may arise; but when an opportunity comes, under the pretext of anger, erotic passion, or something else, they suddenly assault the body by a sword, a noose, a precipice, or some other means. And, after entering the purifying fire, as we said, they put the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them in a state of being punished to the end. Others, being ambushed in another way, do not approach us, because they are deceived by the thoughts of the wicked demons into supposing that they suffer these things from their own gods because of their neglect toward them, that they can reconcile those gods through sacrifices, and that they must not approach us but, on the contrary, must flee and hate us. And all the same, they hate and flee those who have greater compassion for them and pursue them in order to benefit them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐδὲ ὅτι εἰσὶν ἐνφαίνοντες","chosen":"At first they do not even reveal that they exist","rationale":"τὴν ἀρχήν can mean “at the beginning” or idiomatically “at all”; the subsequent εὐκαίρως favors a temporal contrast between initial concealment and later action."},{"source_quote":"εὐκαίρως δὲ ὀργῆς προφάσει, ἔρωτος ἢ ἄλλου τινός","chosen":"when an opportunity comes, under the pretext of anger, erotic passion, or something else","rationale":"ἔρως here denotes passionate or erotic desire, while πρόφασις presents these emotions as occasions or pretexts for the attack."},{"source_quote":"τὸ σῶμα αἰφνιδίως ἐνυβρίζουσιν","chosen":"they suddenly assault the body","rationale":"ἐνυβρίζω conveys violent mistreatment or outrage; “assault” preserves the physical force without specifying a mechanism beyond the list that follows."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τέλος κολασθησομένας","chosen":"in a state of being punished to the end","rationale":"εἰς τέλος may mean “to the end,” “completely,” or in some contexts “forever.” The more source-transparent “to the end” avoids resolving its extent beyond the wording supplied."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἔφαμεν, εἰς τὸ καθάρσιον χωρήσαντες πῦρ","chosen":"after entering the purifying fire, as we said","rationale":"χωρήσαντες is nominative masculine plural and therefore most directly resumes the demons as grammatical subject. Associating the movement conceptually with the mingled people or their souls is possible in context but is less straightforward morphologically."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς μισοῦσιν καὶ φεύγουσιν","chosen":"And all the same, they hate and flee","rationale":"ὁμῶς can mean alike or all the same. The latter preserves the ironic contrast with the compassion shown by those whom they avoid."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.14","text":"Thus, by hating and fleeing us, they are ensnared, not knowing from what source it comes about that they think things contrary to their own salvation. For neither can we compel them, when they are unwilling, to incline toward salvation—since we do not now have such authority over them—nor can they by themselves recognize the demon’s evil thought, for they do not know from where the thoughts of evil are suggested to them. These are the people whom the demons terrify by appearing in whatever forms they wish. Sometimes they also prescribe treatments for the sick, and in this way they gain among those already deceived a reputation as gods and conceal from most people that they are demons—but not from us, who know their secret, the reason why they do such things, transforming themselves in dreams against those over whom they have authority. Some they terrify; to others they issue oracles, demand sacrifices, and command them to share a feast, so that they may drink down their souls along with them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς σωτηρίαν νεῦσαι","chosen":"to incline toward salvation","rationale":"νεύω depicts leaning, inclining, or signaling assent; the phrase concerns an unwilling movement toward salvation rather than physical motion alone."},{"source_quote":"τὴν κακὴν τοῦ δαίμονος ἐνθύμησιν","chosen":"the demon’s evil thought","rationale":"ἐνθύμησις can denote a thought, consideration, or inward suggestion. The possessive construction identifies the demon as its source."},{"source_quote":"θεραπείας συντάσσουσιν","chosen":"prescribe treatments","rationale":"συντάσσω can mean arrange or prescribe, and θεραπεία here refers to treatment or care for the sick."},{"source_quote":"θεῶν δόξαν ἀποφέρονται","chosen":"they gain ... a reputation as gods","rationale":"δόξα here is reputation or estimation, while the genitive θεῶν expresses the status attributed to them."},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτοὺς κατ’ ὄναρ καθ’ ὧν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσι μεταμορφοῦντες","chosen":"transforming themselves in dreams against those over whom they have authority","rationale":"The first κατά marks the dream setting; the second naturally has the adversative sense “against.” An alternative is to understand the second phrase more generally as referring to those subject to their power."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα αὐτῶν τὰς ψυχὰς συνπίνωσιν","chosen":"so that they may drink down their souls along with them","rationale":"The souls are the accusative object of συνπίνωσιν. The compound evokes drinking together at the feast while also portraying the demons as consuming the participants’ souls."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.15","text":"For just as formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths, so these demons also draw those who partake of their table into their own will, having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink. They transform themselves in dreams according to the likenesses of the carved images in order to increase the deception. For the carved image is neither a living creature nor does it possess a divine spirit; rather, the demon that was seen made use of its form. To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams, yet when those people met one another while awake and compared what they had seen in the dream, they did not agree? Consequently, such an appearance is no longer merely something that might appear in a dream; rather, it either belongs to a demon or consists of the soul’s products, as the soul gives the forms back to the pariai fears and to desire. For when struck in its mind by fear, it gives birth to the forms through dreams. But if you think that the carved images, since they are animate, can perform such things, set them on a balance when its beam is level, place the counterweight on the other pan, and call upon them to become either heavier or lighter. If that happens, they are animate; but it does not happen. If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god. For even this can happen by the finger of a demon. Worms also move, and they are not called gods.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δεινοὶ ὄφεις τοῖς αὐτῶν πνεύμασιν τοὺς στρουθοὺς ἐπισπῶνται","chosen":"formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths","rationale":"πνεύματα here are the snakes’ breaths or exhalations, and στρουθοί most naturally denotes sparrows or small birds."},{"source_quote":"διά γε τῶν βρωτῶν καὶ ποτῶν ἀνακραθέντες αὐτῶν τῷ νῷ","chosen":"having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink","rationale":"ἀνακραθέντες portrays the demons as becoming mixed with the participants’ minds by means of what is eaten and drunk."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὰς τῶν ξοάνων ἰδέας","chosen":"according to the likenesses of the carved images","rationale":"ξόανον is a carved cult image, often wooden, while ἰδέαι here are its visible forms or likenesses."},{"source_quote":"πόσοις κατ’ ὄναρ ὁμοίως ἄλλοις ὤφθησαν καὶ ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις πρὸς τὸ κατ’ ὄναρ ἀντιβάλλοντες οὐ συνεφώνησαν;","chosen":"To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams, yet when those people met one another while awake and compared what they had seen in the dream, they did not agree?","rationale":"The nominative participles introduce the dreamers as the understood subjects after πόσοις ἄλλοις. ὕπαρ contrasts waking experience with dreaming, and ἀντιβάλλω denotes comparison."},{"source_quote":"ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν, ἀλλ’ ἢ δαίμονός ἐστιν ἢ ψυχῆς τὰ ἐπιγενήματα","chosen":"Consequently, such an appearance is no longer merely something that might appear in a dream; rather, it either belongs to a demon or consists of the soul’s products","rationale":"The clause shifts between singular and plural predicates and uses optative ἐπιφανείη. The rendering preserves the contrast between demonic agency and products generated by the soul; “it is not a dream apparition” is a possible smoother alternative."},{"source_quote":"διὰ ὀνείρων τὰς ἰδέας ἀποκυΐσκει","chosen":"it gives birth to the forms through dreams","rationale":"ἀποκυΐσκω uses the image of conceiving or giving birth, here applied to the soul’s production of dream forms."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δὲ ἔσται, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν","chosen":"If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god","rationale":"The selected text and punctuation present this as a statement. The surrounding reductio could support taking it rhetorically as “is such a thing therefore a god?”, but that question is not imposed on the main text."},{"source_quote":"καὶ γὰρ δακτύλῳ δαίμονος τοῦτο γενέσθαι δύναται","chosen":"For even this can happen by the finger of a demon","rationale":"The phrase retains the concrete image of a demon’s finger as the means by which the apparent change could be produced."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ","issue":"The printed παρίᾳ does not yield a defensible construction with the plural article and noun in τοῖς ... φόβοις, nor does it provide a secure lexical meaning in context. The translation therefore transliterates it as “pariai” rather than silently omitting or conjecturally replacing it. Because no defensible English meaning can be established for this surviving printed word, this remains a publication-blocking source problem.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
